method: Batting average is hits divided by at-bats. On-base percentage is (hits + walks + hit by pitch) divided by (at-bats + walks + hit by pitch + sacrifice flies). Slugging percentage is total bases divided by at-bats, where total bases count one per single, two per double, three per triple and four per home run, so singles are hits minus doubles, triples and home runs. OPS is on-base percentage plus slugging percentage. Every rate is computed in double precision and reported to three decimals; the page shows baseball's usual style without a leading zero below one. Each count is a whole number from 0 to 20,000, at-bats starts at 1, hits cannot exceed at-bats and extra-base hits cannot exceed hits. Reaching base on an error, catcher's interference, sacrifice bunts and fielder's choice are outside the modelled plate-appearance count, and no park, league or era adjustment is applied.

sources.title: Major League Baseball official rules, Rule 9.21: batting average and slugging percentage from at-bats and total bases
Major League Baseball official rules, Rule 9.22: on-base percentage uses hits, walks and hit-by-pitch over at-bats, walks, hit-by-pitch and sacrifice flies
